prerequisites: It is recommended to take the Statics course.

learning_outcomes.text: Examines normal stresses and deformations caused by axial loading.
Examines stresses under axial loading and shear force.
Calculates shear stresses and deformations under torsional load.
Calculates normal and shear stresses resulting from bending moment and shear forces in beams.

syllabus_topics: Review of Static Methods (Reaction forces and moments), Introduction to Mechanics, Fundamental Concepts and Principles (Basic Physics and Newton's Laws)
Mathematics Required for Mechanics (Algebra and Calculus), Concept of Stress: Axial Loading (Normal and Shear Stresses)

Mathematics Required for Mechanics (Geometry, Trigonometry, and Vectors), Concept of Stress (Continuation): Normal and Shear Stress Applications, Stress on Oblique Sections and Stress under General Loading Conditions, Stress Components
Stress and Strain - Axial Loading: Stress and Strain Diagrams, Hooke's Law, Elastic-Plastic Behavior, Fatigue, Deformation, Statically Indeterminate Systems, Temperature Change
Stress and Strain - Axial Loading (Continuation): Poisson's Ratio, Generalized Hooke's Law, Bulk Modulus, Shear Strain, Saint-Venant's Principle, Stress Concentrations
Torsion: Stresses in Torsion, Deformations in Circular Shafts, Stresses in the Elastic Region, Angle of Twist in the Elastic Region

Torsion (Continuation): Torsion Applications, Statically Indeterminate Shafts in Torsion, Design of Transmission Shafts, Stress Concentrations in Circular Shafts, Torsion of Non-Circular Elements, Torsion of Thin-Walled Hollow Shafts
Simple Bending: Symmetric Element and Deformations, Stress and Deformations in the Elastic Region, Deformations in Transverse Section, Bending of Composite Beams
Simple Bending (Continuation): Bending Applications, Stress Concentrations and Topic Review
Analysis and Design of Beams in Bending: Review of Centroids and Area Moments of Inertia and Shear Force - Bending Moment Diagrams

Analysis and Design of Beams in Bending (Continuation): Transverse Loading, SFD and BMD Diagrams_Distributed Load, Relationships between Shear Force & Bending Moment; Design of Prismatic Beams in Bending, Normal Stress by Area Method & Applications
Analysis and Design of Beams in Bending (Continuation): Use of Area Method and Singularity Functions to Determine Shear Force and Bending Moment in Beams, Non-Prismatic Beams

Shear Stresses in Beams and Thin-Walled Elements: Shear Force on Horizontal Surface of Beam Element, Shear Stresses in Beams, τxy Shear Stress in Common Beam Types, Stress Distribution in Narrow Rectangular Beams, Longitudinal Shear Force in an Arbitrary Beam Element, Shear Stress in Thin-Walled Elements
assessment_rules: The overall grade is calculated based on 50% for in-term activities and 50% for the final exam. In-term activities consist of a midterm exam (90%) and a quiz (10%).
bibliography: Cisimlerin Mukavemeti, Ferdinand P. Beer ve Russell Johnston, 2014 Literatür Yayınları
